extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, participating employers, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), Office of Apprenticeship (OA), and other stakeholders responding to the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the proposed rule's substantive requirements and associated implementation guidance/cost assumptions for registered apprenticeship programs, SAAs, OA, and participating employers (including CTE-specific provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of standards of apprenticeship (§29.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must provide information on standards of apprenticeship to OA (proposed §29.8(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates a Training and Development Manager (private sector) would spend 0.33 hour to provide information on standards of apprenticeship. This estimate aligns with the EEO Supporting Statement; Department seeks public comment on the estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide additional apprentice data (§29.25(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must provide additional data on apprentices to OA as required by proposed §29.25(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates office/administrative support would spend 0.083 hour (5 minutes) per apprentice providing additional data; aligns with EEO Supporting Statement; Department seeks public comment. Costing examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide apprenticeship agreement (§29.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must provide the apprenticeship agreement (proposed §29.9) to OA as part of reporting/registration obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates 0.083 hour (5 minutes) per apprentice by office/administrative support to provide the apprenticeship agreement; aligns with EEO Supporting Statement; Department seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide additional employer data (§29.25(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must provide additional data on participating employers in their programs as required by proposed §29.25(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates office/administrative support would spend 0.083 hour (5 minutes) per participating employer; aligns with EEO Supporting Statement; Department seeks public comment. Costing examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program registration information requirements (§29.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors that submit new applications must include additional information in their applications including a narrative on how they are working with the workforce system, information on financial capacity and other resources to operate the proposed program, and any history of violations; OA and SAAs review this information when making registration determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates sponsors' Training and Development Manager would spend 1 hour submitting the additional information. SAAs' Training and Development Manager estimated to spend 0.5 hour reviewing; OA GS-13 employee estimated to spend 0.5 hour reviewing. Department seeks public comment and provides year-1 cost calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program standards adoption agreement reporting (§29.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-collectively bargained programs must include requirements that participating employers adopt and comply with the sponsor's standards of apprenticeship and applicable requirements under 29 CFR part 30, and sponsors must transmit these adoption agreements to OA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates Training and Development Manager (private sector) would spend 1 hour transmitting adoption agreements to OA; estimate based on program experience and Department seeks public comment. Costing and annualized cost estimates provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Occupational Standards and Program Standards (§§29.13–29.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: OA may create National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship suitable for adoption by program sponsors; these must meet the new standards of proposed §29.7 and characterize competency-based occupational frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates a GS-13 employee would require 40 hours to commission each new national occupational standard; provides cost per standard and annualized totals; seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-point assessments requirement (§29.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must conduct an end-point assessment with the apprentice after completion of the registered apprenticeship program to objectively measure acquisition of relevant knowledge, skills, and competencies; Registration Agency awards a Certificate of Completion after successful completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates apprentices spend 1 hour completing the assessment; sponsors' Training and Development Manager spend 1 hour assessing; Registration Agency GS-7 staff spend 0.25 hour per program to award certificate. Department bases estimates on program experience, seeks public comment, and provides detailed cost and annualized totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of end-point assessments and safety records (§29.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating employers must record and maintain additional information on end-point assessments and safety records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates office/administrative support staff would spend 4 hours recording and maintaining additional information; estimate based on program experience; Department seeks public comment and provides cost estimates and annualized totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic program reviews and Notice of Program Review Findings (§29.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies must conduct periodic program reviews at least every 5 years (off-site desk audits or on-site reviews), may examine/copy documents or interview, and must present a Notice of Program Review Findings to the sponsor. Sponsors receiving a Notice indicating failure of compliance must develop a compliance action plan detailing commitment to remediate deficiencies, precise actions, timeframe, and responsible individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes 20% of sponsors reviewed annually (5-year cycle), with OA and SAAs splitting reviews per historical proportions; estimates reviewer time (GS-13/Training and Development Manager 40 hours per review). Department assumes 20% of sponsors found noncompliant and estimates sponsor burden to develop compliance action plan (8 hours to write plus 0.17 hour to submit). Estimates align with 2016 RIA; Department seeks public comment and provides costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing from SAAs to OA (§29.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: SAAs must furnish OA with apprenticeship-related data applicable to proposed §§29.25 and 29.28; this includes compiling and submitting apprenticeship data and using RAPIDS where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most SAAs already use RAPIDS and face no software costs; three SAAs not using RAPIDS would face one-time software/IT infrastructure and licensing costs and ongoing consulting/maintenance costs. Department estimates staff burdens: Training and Development Manager 32 hours compiling/submitting, 3 computer systems analysts 80 hours each, office/admin support 72 hours; provides per-SAA cost calculations, annualized totals, and seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA reciprocity process and reciprocity statement (§29.26(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain or maintain full or provisional recognition status, SAAs must establish a process and criteria for providing approval to apprentices, apprenticeship programs, and standards of apprenticeship, and must develop and write a reciprocity statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates each SAA's Training and Development Manager would spend 4 hours developing and writing the reciprocity statement; treated as a one-time cost with calculated first-year and annualized costs; Department seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of State Apprenticeship Plan every 4 years (§29.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each SAA must submit a State Apprenticeship Plan every 4 years containing strategic planning elements (goals for expansion; promotion of DEIA; narrative describing workforce development activities; strategy/initiatives for ensuring high-quality apprenticeships), operational planning elements (regulatory documentation, State EEO plan, complaint investigation plan, technical assistance plan, performance reporting process, program review plan, registration standards, reciprocity policy, data sharing policy), and assorted assurances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates Training and Development Manager (State level) would spend 86 hours to develop, write, review, and submit the plan; aligns with WIOA State Plans supporting statement; periodic cost occurs every 4 years with year-specific and annualized cost estimates; Department seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE rule familiarization (one-time) for sponsors, employers, SAAs
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed rule becomes final, registered CTE apprenticeship program sponsors, participating employers, and SAAs must familiarize themselves with the new regulation, incurring a one-time cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates Training and Development Manager (private sector) for sponsors spends 4 hours; participating employers' Training and Development Manager spends 2 hours; CTE SAAs' Training and Development Manager spends 4 hours. Estimates align with past RIA assumptions; costs provided for year 1 and subsequent years for new entrants; Department seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of industry skills frameworks (§29.24(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: OA must develop industry skills frameworks: training outlines that describe core competencies across an industry and specify on-the-job training outlines with minimum on-the-job training hours to meet industry benchmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes frameworks for 16 industries, GS-13 employee 80 hours per industry to develop training material/content, expects 8 frameworks/year in years 1–2, and industry leaders will spend ~2 hours reviewing each framework. Cost calculations and annualized totals provided; Department seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic CTE apprenticeship program registration applications (§29.24(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective CTE program sponsors must electronically submit to a Registration Agency an application that includes written plans and assurances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department anticipates the sponsor's Training and Development Manager would spend 10 hours compiling and submitting the application; estimate based on program experience; Department provides year-by-year cost examples and seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of a diverse and inclusive cross-section of students (§29.24(d)(2)(v)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors must ensure a diverse and inclusive cross-section of students is selected for participation (e.g., outreach to underserved communities and regular distribution of information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes program sponsors' HR manager and administrative assistant each spend 0.5 hours distributing information to underserved communities; estimate aligns with 2016 EEO RIA outreach assumptions; Department provides cost estimates and seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor oversight of participating employers (§29.24(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors must ensure each participating employer adheres to all requirements of the proposed rule (oversight responsibilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department anticipates the sponsor's HR manager would spend 8 hours performing oversight duties; estimate based on program experience; Department provides cost calculations and seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship agreement requirement (§29.24(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: All program sponsors registered by a Registration Agency must develop and establish a written CTE apprenticeship agreement that contains terms and conditions of employment, education, and training of the CTE apprentice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department anticipates Training and Development Manager (private sector) would spend 0.167 hours preparing/signing the CTE apprenticeship agreement; aligns with prior IRAP rule estimates; Department provides cost estimates and seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credentials upon completion of CTE program (§29.24(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies must provide a nationally recognized certificate of completion for registered CTE apprenticeship and any other industry-recognized credential to students who meet graduation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates OA (41.8% of credentials) would have a GS-13 employee spend 0.25 hour per credential; SAAs (58.2%) would have a Training and Development Manager spend 0.25 hour per credential. Assumptions on proportion of credentials, timing (first cohort in year 2), and cost calculations provided; Department seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE program registration timeliness and notification (§29.24(g)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies must review CTE apprenticeship program registration applications and determine eligibility for registration within 90 days of receipt, and must inform applicants in writing of decisions regarding program registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department anticipates GS-13 (OA) and Training and Development Manager (SAAs) would each spend 2 hours reviewing applications and informing applicants; estimate based on program experience; cost examples and annualized totals provided; Department seeks public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance and outreach for CTE adoption (§29.24(g)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies must provide outreach, technical assistance, and other support to potential sponsors to support adoption of registered CTE apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates OA would provide technical assistance to 41.8% of program sponsors (per registration proportions) and that a GS-13 employee would spend approximately 3 hours providing technical assistance; estimates align with 2016 WIOA RIA assumptions; Department provides costing and seeks public comment.
